bull_bear.body: Paid interim dividend of Rs.37.7cr and special dividend of Rs.101.55cr (Rs.22.50/share); net cash position of Rs.226cr; inorganic growth remains strategic priority, no constraint due to strong balance sheet
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: North American large Ag continued softness; global economic slowdown; geopolitical tensions; tariff volatility; rupee appreciation reversing FX benefits
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and strategic; emphasizes operational resilience, dual-shore advantage, disciplined capital allocation, and inorganic growth pipeline; tone is upbeat on construction and European Ag, cautious on NA large Ag
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Mexico warehouse commissioning (Oct 2025) is a hidden catalyst for tariff mitigation and customer retention; 25% flat tariff on tractor parts (Oct 31) is a positive inflection for US aftermarket, not yet priced in
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- 'Our net cash position at the end of Q1 stands at INR 190 crore, reflecting the continued strength of our cash generation'; 'Our balance sheet is in excellent health'.
- 'When we declared the special dividend of INR 101cr in October 2025, our cash balance was approximately INR 210 crore. In ten months, through focussed operations and business growth, we have rebuilt to that level.'
- Debt/Equity has risen steadily but stays low: 0.02x FY23, 0.07x FY24, 0.09x FY25, 0.11x FY26.
- Returns on a trailing twelve-month basis per management: 'our EPS stands at INR 39.97, and our ROCE is north of 27%, with ROE at 20%'.
- Cash Flow from Operations has declined each year on the deck's own chart: INR 2,527 Mn FY23, 1,997 Mn FY24, 1,820 Mn FY25, 1,736 Mn FY26.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Construction: 40-45% of revenue, green (strong growth from US AI infra & EU green energy); Large Ag: 17-20%, red in NA (soft), amber in EU (recovering); Small Ag: ~25%, green in Asia/India (GST cut boost), amber in NA (bottoming); Aftermarket: single-digit growth, subdued in EU (inventory), improving in US post-Oct 31 tariff ruling
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- 'Market leaders in small tractor (<70 HP) linkage system globally' and 'Leading global supplier in fragmented market with manufacturing base in India and US and servicing all major geographies (Americas, Europe, Japan, India, ROW)'.
- 'Servicing all 10 leading Global OHV OEMs in Agriculture and half of the leading 10 players in the CFM Segment' (footnoted as 'CFM global players outside China').
- Moat framed around product character: 'Complex, critical, and low volume high SKUs products'; 'Involved from the design stage for new products and launches providing end-to-end solutions'; 'Preferred component supplier for manufacturer of <70 HP Tractors'.
- Relationship depth: 'Four of the Top Five Customers have been Associated with Uniparts for over 10 years'; '~45% staff members working with Uniparts Group for 10+ years'; '250+ Engineers / Technical Diploma holders' and a '50+ strong Business Development and Sales / Customer Service organization'.
- Market size cited on the 3PL/PMP slide as '$1 billion+'.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Order book] 'Our trailing twelve-month new business order book remains robust at over INR 225 crore, with a healthy pipeline. These wins span segments and geographies... The new business momentum is structural, and we intend to build on it.'
- [Customer concentration] The concentration chart reads top customer 28% / 27% / 31%, top 5 customers 61% / 64% / 71%, top 10 customers 76% / 78% / 84% across FY25 / FY26 / Q1FY27 - i.e. concentration stepping up in Q1FY27.
- [End markets] Construction equipment momentum from H2 CY2025 continues, supported by US technology-investment-led and European government-led infrastructure spending; large agriculture 'remains subdued', with leading OEMs indicating 'CY2026 represents the cyclical bottom, with a more meaningful recovery expected through CY2027'; western small ag is turning after 'three consecutive years of volume declines'.
- [Tariffs] 'Tariff-driven price volatility has led to some demand skewing, as higher prices caused customers and channel partners to moderate their purchasing. With tariffs having since come down, we expect this to normalise and the segment to return to growth.'
- [Certification] Milestones cite '3 units SER certified by Caterpillar' (2024) and 'Two factories SER certified by Caterpiller second year in a row' (2025); the covering exchange letter describes the company as 'An ISO 9001:2008 & 14001:2004 Company'.
- [Group structure] Uniparts India Ltd. sits above Gripwel Fasteners Pvt. Ltd. (GFPL), Gripwel Conag Pvt. Ltd. (GCPL), Uniparts USA Ltd. (UUL), Uniparts India GmbH (UIG) and Uniparts Olsen Inc (UOI); only two 100% holdings are marked and the extract does not bind them to specific entities.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Gross margin expansion driven by 85-90% FX benefit (INR depreciation vs USD/EUR); remaining 10-15% from product mix and tariff pass-throughs; normalized EBITDA margin target: 18-20%
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: mid-teen % for FY26; margin: targeting 18-20% normalized EBITDA; order inflow: Rs.200cr annualized new awards; capex/commissioning: Rs.6cr in Q2, Mexico warehouse operational since Oct 2025
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Rs.200cr annualized new business awards over past 12 months; construction and European Ag driving new wins
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Expansion into hydraulics, large fabrications, PTOs via inorganic acquisitions; untapped potential in oil & gas, industrial machinery, mining (under construction segment); Asia and Europe as key growth corridors
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Uniparts delivered 14.6% YoY revenue growth and 22.6% EBITDA margin driven by rupee depreciation and Mexico warehouse commissioning, with construction and European Ag outperforming North American Ag; the normalized margin is 18-20%, and FY27 growth is expected to accelerate as markets recover.
